transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Name]. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, Doc. Well, what brings me in is... I just keep planning my whole day around not having to drive over those high bridges. It's turning into a real hassle. Like, I work in HR over at the warehouse, and my normal route would take me right over the river. We actually just wrapped up open enrollment for the benefits, which is always a complete nightmare. You wouldn't believe how many people just don't read the forms. I mean, they just check boxes without looking. I had this one guy last week who accidentally dropped his dental coverage and then came into my office yelling at me about it like I did it. 

But anyway, yeah, the bridges. If I can't find a backroad to get around it, I just white-knuckle it the whole way across. Just gripping the wheel for dear life until I'm on solid ground again. My car's an older Chevy, and I swear I'm wearing the material right off the steering wheel from holding it so tight. Needs an oil change soon, too, now that I think about it... I usually take it to that spot on 4th Street, they always have a coupon.
Do you feel a strong fear or anxiety specifically when you have to drive over high bridges, and does that lead you to go out of your way to avoid them?

Yeah, exactly. I mean, I know those bridges over the bay are built fine, right? Folks drive them every single day without a problem. But when I get near one, my mind just acts like the car could go right over the side. It's crazy. Speaking of cars, my brother-in-law just bought one of those new electric ones. The ones where you don't even need gas? He brought it over on Sunday to show it off, and I gotta tell you, it's weird not hearing the engine start. He says he saves a ton on gas, but then you gotta install that charging thing in your garage. My garage is so full of junk right now anyway, I don't even know where I'd put a charger. I've been meaning to have a garage sale since last summer, but who has the time? 

But yeah, I do go out of my way to avoid the bridges. I'll take the long way around, even if it adds twenty minutes to the drive. Better than feeling like I'm gonna drive right off the edge.
Do you ever feel this kind of anxiety or fear in other situations, or is it mostly just when you're driving over high bridges?

No, it's really just the bridges. I don't have a problem with heights or anything like that. Like, I can go up in a tall building no problem. Actually, my sister works in one of those high-rises downtown, up on the 32nd floor. I went up there for her retirement party last month. They had this huge spread, catered by that Italian place on Main Street. The meatballs were incredible, but the pasta was a little cold. Anyway, she finally retired after thirty years at the same firm. They gave her a watch, which I thought was a little cliché, you know? But she seemed to like it. She's moving down to Florida next week. The humidity down there is awful, I don't know how she's gonna stand it. I went down there for a vacation back in '98 and I swear I sweat through three shirts a day. But yeah, no, just the bridges. Everything else is fine.
When you drive over a high bridge or think about doing so, do you ever feel sudden physical symptoms like a racing heart, sweating, shaking, or shortness of breath?

Yeah, I definitely get that. It's like... as soon as I see the bridge coming up in the distance, my chest just gets so tight. My hands start sweating all over the steering wheel, and I just lock my eyes straight ahead, thinking, "I just gotta make it to the other side." Speaking of making it to the other side, they're doing all that construction on Interstate 80 right now, and man, the traffic is just backed up for miles. I sat in it for an hour yesterday just trying to get to the hardware store. I needed some of that special sealant for the gutters. You know, the kind that comes in the silver tube? We had a huge storm last week and the wind blew half the leaves from the Miller's yard right into my gutters. Jim Miller, he's a nice guy, but he never rakes his yard. He's always out there tinkering with his boat instead. He's got this old pontoon he's trying to fix up for the summer. But anyway, yeah, the sweating and the tight chest, it happens right away when I see the bridge.
Does this fear of driving over high bridges cause you a lot of distress or interfere with your daily activities, such as work or social plans?

Well, I mean, I still get to work and I still see my friends and everything. It's not like I'm locked in the house. But I do have to leave extra early for things because I'm taking the long way around to avoid those bridges. Like I said, it adds twenty minutes, sometimes more if there's traffic. And it does bug me, you know? It makes me feel... I don't know, less independent than I used to be. Like I can't just hop in the car and go wherever I want without planning out a whole route first. 

Actually, it's funny you mention social plans, because I've had to turn down a couple of fishing outings with the guys from work lately. We usually go up to Lake Winnebago in the spring, but the best way up there goes right over that huge suspension bridge. The guys were giving me a hard time about it, saying I was getting soft in my old age. Speaking of old age, my knees have been killing me lately. I think it's from standing so much at the office. We've got this new filing system in HR and I swear I'm up and down from my desk fifty times a day. I tried taking some of that glucosamine stuff my neighbor recommended, but I don't think it's doing a darn thing. He swears by it, though. He's this retired postal worker, walks his dog past my house every morning at exactly 6:15. You could set your watch by him. But yeah, the bridge thing... it's a hassle, for sure. I just wish I could drive over them like a normal person.
Have you ever had sudden episodes of intense fear or physical symptoms like a racing heart or shortness of breath when you weren't near a high bridge or driving at all?

No, no, I haven't had anything like that happen anywhere else. It's really just the bridges. If I'm sitting at home or working at the office, I'm perfectly fine. Well, I mean, as fine as you can be with these knees, right? I was telling my wife just the other night—we were sitting on the porch, having a glass of iced tea. She makes this incredible sun tea, leaves it out on the back deck all afternoon with a couple of lemon slices. It's the only thing that gets me through these hot afternoons. Anyway, I was telling her that if my knees keep acting up, I might have to look into getting one of those ergonomic chairs for my desk. The ones they have in the HR department right now are just awful. They're these cheap plastic things they bought in bulk back in, what, 2015? The cushioning is completely gone. I brought in a pillow from home just to have some support. It's this ugly plaid thing, but it does the trick. But no, to answer your question, no sudden panic or anything like that unless there's a bridge involved.
Do you worry that you might lose control or have a panic attack while driving over a high bridge, even if you're not currently feeling those symptoms?

Well, yeah, I guess I do worry about that. It's always in the back of my mind, you know? Like, what if I'm halfway across and my hands just freeze up, or I can't catch my breath, and I end up causing a huge pileup? That's actually why I started taking the long way around in the first place, just to avoid even the chance of that happening. Speaking of taking the long way, they finally finished paving that stretch of Route 9 down by the old lumber yard. Man, that took them forever. I swear they had the cones out for six months, and nobody was ever working when I drove by. It's like they just put the cones up and went on vacation. My buddy Phil used to work for the county highway department, and he said they always drag those jobs out just to keep the budget up for the next year. Phil's a character, though. He retired a couple years back and bought this massive RV. He and his wife just drive around the country now. They send me postcards from all these random places, like the world's biggest ball of twine or whatever. He was trying to get me to buy an RV too, but I don't know, with gas prices the way they are, and then you gotta find a place to park the thing... I don't think my wife would go for it anyway. She likes her own bed too much. But yeah, the worry about losing control on a bridge, it's definitely there. It's just not something I want to risk.
Have you ever experienced these panic-like symptoms in any other specific situations besides driving over high bridges, such as in crowds, public transportation, or open spaces?

No, nothing like that. It's really just the bridges. Crowds don't bother me, and I take the bus downtown sometimes when there's a baseball game, no problem at all. Speaking of the bus, they just changed the schedule on the 42 line that runs past my neighborhood. Used to be every twenty minutes, now it's every half hour. Really messes up my timing if I'm trying to catch it. I ran into my neighbor down at the stop the other day—the postal worker, you know? He was telling me they're talking about raising the fare again. It's ridiculous. I mean, they raise the fare, but the buses are still late, and half the time the air conditioning doesn't even work. He said he heard it from a guy who works down at the transit authority. But yeah, no, I'm fine in crowds and on buses and all that. Just the bridges.
